config.title: Quiet Hours in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: When Berlin's protected quiet hours actually apply, what the house rulebook can and cannot do, and the flat habits that keep a visitor out of trouble.

items.q: What are the quiet hours in Berlin?
items.a: **Berlin's noise law protects the night from 22:00 to 06:00, and Sundays and public holidays for the whole day.** During those periods it is forbidden to cause noise that could seriously disturb another person. There is no decibel threshold in the law and no list of banned devices: the question is whether your neighbour is seriously disturbed. Building sites work to a stricter night of 20:00 to 07:00, which is why scaffolding goes quiet so early in the evening.

items.q: Is there a midday quiet period in Berlin?
items.a: **Not in the state noise law.** If your building posts a Mittagsruhe between 13:00 and 15:00, that is the Hausordnung, the building's own rulebook, which is a private agreement attached to the flat. It can be enforced against your host, and your host can pass that on to you, but a neighbour cannot call the police over it the way they can over a 23:00 speaker. The genuine 13:00 to 15:00 restriction in German federal law applies to outdoor garden and building machinery in residential areas, not to anything happening inside a flat.

items.q: Do Sundays really count all day in Berlin?
items.a: **Yes, and this is the rule visitors miss most often.** Sunday is a legal category in Berlin, not a cultural preference, and the ban on seriously disturbing noise runs from midnight to midnight. Berlin's ten public holidays behave identically. In 2026 that includes 3 October, which falls on a Saturday, so that Saturday follows the Sunday rule. Vacuuming, drilling and moving furniture are the classic Sunday flashpoints.

**Room volume, meaning the sound stays inside your room.** There is no legal number behind the word, which frustrates people who want one. The working test is simple: if a neighbour can follow your music, hear the dialogue of your film, or name the song, you are above it. After 22:00 this is the standard for everything that makes sound on purpose, including a video call on laptop speakers. Older Berlin buildings carry sound through the floorboards and ventilation shafts much better than a modern hotel does.

items.q: Can I shower at night in a Berlin flat?
items.a: **Yes.** Washing at night is ordinary use of a home, and German courts have repeatedly refused to enforce house rules that tried to ban night-time showering or bathing, treating roughly half an hour as normal household noise. It is one of the odder facts about Berlin flats: the thing that feels rude at 01:00 is allowed, while one speaker on a kitchen table is the thing with a fine attached to it.

items.q: Why does the courtyard matter so much?
items.a: **A Berlin Hinterhof is a stone box open at the top, so it works like a chimney for sound.** Nineteenth-century blocks packed a rear building behind the street building with flats facing in on all four sides, and the walls reflect voices straight back at every window. Four people saying goodnight in the courtyard at 01:00 reach more bedrooms than the same four people on the pavement outside the front door. Step out through the street door and say goodbye there.

items.q: What happens if a neighbour complains about noise?
items.a: **During office hours the district Ordnungsamt is responsible, and in the evening, at night and at weekends the police handle it instead.** The official Berlin service page also asks neighbours to speak to you or to the landlord first, which is why the first contact is almost always a doorbell. If it does become formal, the published bands for private individuals run from 50 to 2,500 euros for night noise and from 40 to 2,000 euros for noise on a Sunday or public holiday, and they are halved where the offence was careless instead of deliberate. Those are catalogue ranges, not the expected outcome of one loud evening. Say sorry, turn it down, and it ends there. Checked on 6 September 2026.

items.q: What is the one habit that prevents most complaints?
items.a: **Carry the suitcase down the stairs instead of wheeling it, and close the front door with your hand on it.** Hard wheels on old stair tiles at 05:30 and a sprung street door slamming into a stone stairwell are the two loudest things most visitors do, and both take seconds to avoid. Add one more: put anything loud, laundry, a repack, moving furniture, into daylight on a weekday.
